newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES GIVES U.S. FIRST POINT OF FED CUP FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES GIVES U.S. FIRST POINT OF FED CUP FINAL.

text.p: Monica Seles put the United States in front in the Fed Cup final with Spain by beating Conchita Martinez 6-2 6-4 in the opening singles match on Saturday.
In a rematch of the U.S. Open semifinal played three weeks ago, the co-world number one ran her perfect record against the Spaniard to 10-0.

Seles throughly dominated the first set with a very effective serve and extremely deep groundstrokes against a Martinez who appeared ready to concede the first point of the best-of-five championship from the outset.
Seles showed no sign of the shoulder injury that has hampered her serve in recent months, winning all four of her first-set service games at love.
Martinez woke up in the second set to make a match of it.
The Spaniard began playing far more aggressively and broke Seles in the opening game to put some pressure on the Yugoslav-born American.

Martinez was playing by far her best tennis of the match towards the end and saved two match points in the spirited final game. But it was too little, too late for the fourth-ranked Spaniard, who was simply outgunned by the power-hitting number one.
Saturday's second singles match is a rematch of the Atlanta Olympic final with American gold medalist Lindsay Davenport facing Spain's silver medalist Arantxa Sanchez Vicario.
Spain is aiming for its fourth consecutive Fed Cup title and third at the expense of the Americans. The United States last won the Fed Cup in 1990.
Sunday's format features the two reverse singles matches followed by doubles.
Davenport later shook off a slow start to overwhelm Spain's number one Sanchez 7-5 6-1 in just 64 minutes, giving the United States a commanding 2-0 lead.
Sanchez, knowing Spain needed a victory to keep alive a realistic chance of holding onto the Cup, jumped out to a 5-3 lead over the Olympic champion.
But the American settled down and cranked her game up several notches, running off seven consecutive games and 10 of the last 11 from a stunned Sanchez.
The United States now has three chances on Sunday to avenge Fed Cup defeats of the last two years.
Seles will get the first chance to close it out when she plays Sanchez in the first reverse singles match.
Davenport then takes on Martinez before Davenport and Mary Joe Fernandez team up for doubles against the Spanish duo that has carried Spain to its sixth consecutive Fed Cup finals.
